memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, he anointed and consecrated it and all its furnishings. He also anointed and consecrated the altar and all its utensils. Then the leaders of Israel, the heads of families who were the tribal leaders in charge of those who were counted, made offerings. They brought as their gifts before the Lord six covered carts and twelve oxen—an ox from each leader and a cart from every two. These they presented before the tabernacle. - Num 7:1-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The tabernacle was finished, anointed, and set apart for God. And immediately, the leaders of Israel stepped forward to give. They brought carts and oxen — practical, useful gifts to support the ongoing work of God's dwelling place.

Notice who led the way in giving: the leaders. Those with the most influence set the example of generosity. They did not merely organise others to give; they gave first and gave willingly. True leadership in God's work always includes leading by example, especially in devotion and generosity.

Notice too that the gifts were practical. Carts and oxen are not glamorous, but they were exactly what was needed to carry and maintain the tabernacle as Israel travelled. Sometimes the most God-honouring gifts are the ordinary, useful ones — the practical help that keeps God's work moving forward.

The leaders gave freely, out of glad hearts, at the very start of the tabernacle's service. Their giving was an act of worship, a way of saying, "This work matters, and we want to be part of it."

God still delights in willing givers who support His work with what they have. It may be money, time, skills, or simple practical help. Whatever form it takes, giving to God's work is a privilege, not a burden.

What can you bring today to support the work of God — cheerfully, practically, and from the heart?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you lead by example in generosity?
- What practical gifts can you bring to support God's work?
- Is your giving an act of glad worship?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the privilege of giving to Your work. Make me a willing, cheerful giver, offering both practical help and a devoted heart. Amen.
